notes: Built from the single clean copy in the PDF (one POSITION STATEMENT, Revised 06/15/26, Reviewed 05/28/26; no redline). effective_date is the Revised date; the Original Effective Date printed is 10/15/16.

plan_types: the header says the guideline applies to all lines of business unless noted in Program Exceptions. excluded_plans: FEP follows FEP guidelines, SAO follows SAO guidelines. Medicare Advantage is listed in Program Exceptions only as 'the following NCDs were reviewed' (150.9 Arthroscopic Lavage and Debridement for the Osteoarthritic Knee, 150.12 Collagen Meniscus Implant); the document does not say MA follows them, so MA is not in excluded_plans. A reviewer could read it as a deferral.

Every 'Failure of at least N of conservative non-operative management that includes at least 2 of the following' block is built as all(duration criterion, any(every pair of the six modalities)): 15 pairs. The duration criterion carries the months threshold (6 weeks = 1.5 months); the modality criteria (Medications, assistive device(s), home exercise, physical therapy, therapeutic injections into the joint, activity modification) are shared by every section because they are the same requirement with the same words everywhere (semicolon- or comma-separated).

'Medications (unless contraindicated)' is modelled as any(medications, medications_contraindicated) wherever medications appear: a documented contraindication satisfies the medications item and counts toward the 'at least 2'. The criterion text 'unless contraindicated' is the waiver's own words. Same pattern for '(if not contraindicated)' on the 6-month DMARD trial in the rheumatoid synovitis pathway.

Four duration criteria for conservative management because the wording differs by section: 'at least 3 months' (diagnostic, three debridement pathways, ACL persistent-pain, PCL, painful plica), 'at least 6 weeks' (meniscal acute and repairable, meniscal allograft, proliferative synovial disease), 'at least 6 months' (lateral release) and '6 months' without 'at least' (both patellar realignment pathways). The last two are the same clinical requirement; kept separate to stay verbatim.

Lateral release and the third patellar realignment pathway require management 'that included supervised physical therapy, and at least 1 of' a five-item list (no physical therapy in the list): built as all(duration, supervised_pt, any(five singles)). 'supervised physical therapy' is its own criterion, distinct from the plain 'physical therapy' modality.

'No imaging evidence of meniscus tear, loose body, advanced arthritis (Kellgren grade III or IV), or fracture' (diagnostic arthroscopy) is built as not(any(four leaves)) per the 'none of the following' rule; 'No fracture or loose body by imaging' (patellar realignment) as not(any(fracture, loose body)); 'No patellar dislocation' and 'No evidence of advanced osteoarthritis (Kellgren grade III or IV)' as not(leaf). The leaf texts are the short verbatim fragments ('meniscus tear', 'fracture', 'patellar dislocation'); the questions carry the imaging context. A reviewer could instead keep each 'No ...' sentence as one positive criterion.

The loose body leaf is one criterion ('Imaging documentation of a loose body', from the Loose Body Removal section) used positively there and negated in the diagnostic arthroscopy and patellar realignment pathways: it is the same imaging finding.

Kellgren-Lawrence grade 0-2 is one criterion (text from the PCL bullet 'Absent or minimal osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 0-2)') reused where ACL ('Osteoarthritis is absent or minimal (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 0-2)') and the repairable-tear meniscal pathway ('Xrays demonstrate absent or minimal osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 0-2)') state the same requirement in slightly different words. Likewise 'advanced osteoarthritis (Kellgren grade III or IV)' (patellofemoral chondrosis) stands for the diagnostic section's 'advanced arthritis (Kellgren grade III or IV)', and 'There are mechanical symptoms' is the shared prefix of the OA-debridement sentence ('including, but are not limited to, locking, snapping, or popping') and the microfracture sentence ('including, but not limited to, ...').

'and/or' symptom lists are single criteria (e.g. 'Knee pain, loss of function and/or persistent effusion'; 'Limited range of motion, effusion, and/or painful weight bearing, present for at least 3 months'; 'Presence of pain, stiffness, limited ability to straighten the le.g., limping, and/or swelling') because any one of the listed findings satisfies the bullet; the arthrofibrosis text keeps the PDF's typo 'le.g.,' (for 'leg, e.g.,') to stay verbatim.

Explicit 'OR' alternatives inside one bullet are any nodes with two leaves: 'Normal knee biomechanics, OR alignment and stability will be achieved concurrently with osteochondral grafting' (autografting) and 'Normal knee biomechanics or alignment and stability is present or will be achieved concurrently with meniscal transplantation' (allograft transplant); 'Normal knee biomechanics' is shared. 'Candidate is a skeletally mature adolescent ... OR an adult considered too young ...' is an any of two leaves.

Sentences holding two requirements were split: 'MRI evidence of a tear considered repairable by the surgeon, with pain that corresponds to the location of the tear'; 'A child or adolescent with any type of meniscal tear confirmed on MRI'; 'Persistent pain or loss of knee function with ligament instability or a repairable meniscus' (the pain/function leaf is shared with the second ACL pathway); 'The articular cartilage surrounding the lesion(s) is Outerbridge grade II or less, and normal-appearing hyaline cartilage surrounding the border of the defect'; 'Patellofemoral tenderness and abnormal articulation of the patella'; 'Osteochondral allografting ... Full-thickness chondral defects ... when other cartilage repair techniques ... would be inadequate'. 'Acute injury with onset of pain with twisting/rotation, crepitus, locking, giving way, difficulty straightening, or joint line tenderness' was kept as one criterion (an acute injury presenting with any of those).

Meniscal allograft 'also meets the definition of medical necessity when performed in combination ... with treatment of focal articular cartilage lesions using any of' ACI / osteochondral allografting / osteochondral autografting is built as an independent second pathway (combination criterion + any of three procedures), as printed. A reviewer could read it as requiring the base transplant criteria too.
The PCL section's fourth bullet ('Absent or minimal osteoarthritis') has no trailing AND, but the header says ALL of the following, so it is in the all.

Thresholds: 'e.g.' ages (54 or younger; ≥15 years; ≤55 years) are recorded as numeric thresholds although the document gives them as examples. The osteochondral autograft lesion size 'between 1 and 2.5 cm2' is a range that one threshold op cannot express, so that criterion has no threshold. 'Documented minimal to absent diffuse degenerative changes ... (e.g., Outerbridge grade II or less, <50% joint space narrowing)' carries the Outerbridge example as its threshold; the joint-space example is in the question only. 'At least 3 months have passed since surgery, traumatic injury, or infection' is typed as a duration in months (time since an event, not a treatment trial).

Codes: all table codes are 'covered' except C8003 (table says Investigational; position statement calls the MISHA shock absorber experimental or investigational for any indication). The table ties no code to a section; mapping by procedure described: 29870 diagnostic; 29877 + G0289 the four debridement pathways; G0289 also loose body removal (its descriptor covers both); 27332/27333/27403/29880/29881/29882/29883 meniscectomy and meniscal repair (29880/29881's included chondroplasty is not separately governed); 29868 meniscal allograft transplant; 29888 ACL and 29889 PCL; the open cruciate codes 27407 (cruciate repair), 27409 (collateral and cruciate), 27428/27429 (intra-articular reconstruction) to both ACL and PCL pathways; 27427 (extra-articular augmentation) to ACL only; 29879 microfracture/abrasion/drilling; 27415/29867 osteochondral allografting; 27416/29866 osteochondral autografting; 29875/29876 synovectomy; 29874 loose body removal; 27425/29873 lateral release; 27418/27420/27422/27424 patellar realignment; 29884 lysis of adhesions.

27405 (primary repair, collateral ligament) is in the code table but the position statement has no collateral ligament criteria (the Ligament Reconstruction/Repair heading holds ACL and PCL only), so no pathway names it; it is tagged covered because the document does not say otherwise. 'Debridement for arthrofibrosis' is mapped to the debridement codes (29877, G0289), not to 29884, which has its own Lysis of Adhesions section with stricter criteria.

Left out as not requirements: the Description / Summary and Analysis of Evidence narrative; the Kellgren-Lawrence and Outerbridge grading definitions (read only to type the grade thresholds); 'Refer to section entitled POSITION STATEMENT' under Reimbursement; the step-therapy protocol exemption paragraph (Florida law 627.42393); Related Guidelines (ACI 02-20000-17; Knee Arthroplasty 02-20000-60); committee approval and update history.

exclusions.text: The use of a medial knee implanted shock absorber (e.g., MISHA™ Knee System) for any indication is considered experimental or investigational.
